patches.value: Choose such B from F003. Define the total function v(h,x)=(e(x,t0+h)-e(x,t0))/h when 0<|h|<eta, and v(h,x)=0 otherwise. The density is evaluated only at positive times in the first branch. Define bnd(x)=B 1_Q(x). Q is a measurable box of finite measure by F002; hence bnd is integrable and its absolute integral is B|Q|<∞. For every 0<|h|<eta, H002 makes the two densities in v continuous in x; their scalar difference quotient is continuous and therefore strongly measurable as a real-valued function.

For completeness retain the supplied final conservation statement. Fix arbitrary s,t>0 and use the exhaustive order cases s=t, s<t, or t<s. In the equality branch introduce L0: s=t; substitution gives E(t)=E(s), and discharge L0. In the increasing branch introduce L1: s<t. F002 gives differentiability on (s,t) with derivative zero, and continuity on [s,t], since E is differentiable at every positive time, including the endpoints. Apply M004 to E extended by zero at nonpositive arguments, derivative function identically zero, and endpoints s,t. It gives 0=(E(t)-E(s))/(t-s), hence E(t)=E(s), since t-s>0. Discharge L1. In the decreasing branch introduce L2: t<s. Apply M004 with endpoints t,s and the same functions; it gives 0=(E(s)-E(t))/(s-t), hence E(t)=E(s), since s-t>0. Discharge L2. Each interval lies strictly in (0,∞), so the extension does not affect any value or derivative there. Case elimination gives E(t)=E(s) in all cases; quantifying over s,t proves constancy on (0,∞). Combining this with F002 proves the exported conclusion, with exactly the original density and normalization.
